items.exampleEn: Many cats learn to pee in a box of sand.
items.exampleZh: 很多貓會學著在沙盆裡尿尿。

items.exampleEn: Scientists use microorganisms to clean up oil that spills into the sea.
items.exampleZh: 科學家利用微生物清除流進海裡的石油。

items.exampleEn: This table is made from untreated wood, so it still smells like a forest.
items.exampleZh: 這張桌子是用未經處理的木頭做的，所以聞起來還有森林的味道。

items.exampleEn: Polio mainly affected young children, so it was often called a childhood disease.
items.exampleZh: 小兒麻痺症過去主要影響幼童，所以常被稱為兒童疾病。

items.exampleEn: Influenza spreads quickly in crowded places in winter.
items.exampleZh: 冬天時，流感在人多的地方傳播得很快。

items.exampleEn: Nursing students practice placing an intravenous needle on special models.
items.exampleZh: 護理系學生在特製的模型上練習打靜脈注射針。

items.exampleEn: The bloodstream carries heat as well as oxygen around the body.
items.exampleZh: 血液除了運送氧氣，也把熱量帶到全身。

items.exampleEn: During the operation, the patient needed a blood transfusion.
items.exampleZh: 手術期間，病人需要輸血。

items.sentenceEn: Polio was once common, but today it has almost disappeared.
items.sentenceZh: 小兒麻痺症曾經很常見，如今幾乎已經消失。

items.audioEn: Is there a rest stop soon? The kids need to pee.
items.audioZh: 附近有休息站嗎？孩子們要尿尿。
items.questionZh: 說話者為什麼要找休息站？
options: The car needs more gas soon
They want to eat some lunch

items.sentenceEn: The struggling company received a transfusion of cash from investors.
items.sentenceZh: 那家陷入困境的公司獲得了投資人的一筆資金挹注。

items.sentenceEn: The baby peed right after we changed her clothes.
items.sentenceZh: 我們剛幫寶寶換好衣服，她就尿尿了。

items.stemEn: When you eat sugar, it is quickly absorbed into your ____.
items.stemZh: 吃糖的時候，糖分很快就會被吸收進血液中。

items.stemEn: Every winter, many offices are half empty because of ____.
items.stemZh: 每年冬天，很多辦公室都因為流感而空了一半。

items.passageEn: Last month, our class visited a science museum with a special exhibition on medicine. One room showed how microorganisms were first seen under a microscope. A second display showed herbs that people used as medicine long ago. Another explained how the polio vaccine changed the lives of millions of children. We also learned that influenza changes every year, so scientists must keep updating vaccines. A model of the human body showed how medicine given through an intravenous line enters the bloodstream directly. Near the exit, a poster thanked people who give blood, since they make transfusions possible. Our guide also reminded us that untreated water can carry germs. I left the museum with a new respect for science.
items.passageZh: 上個月，我們班去參觀一間有醫學特展的科學博物館。有一間展示人們最早如何在顯微鏡下看到微生物。有個展區展示古人當作藥用的香草。另一間說明小兒麻痺疫苗如何改變了數百萬兒童的生活。我們也學到流感每年都會變化，所以科學家必須不斷更新疫苗。一個人體模型展示了經由靜脈注射給的藥如何直接進入血液。出口附近有一張海報感謝捐血者，因為有他們的付出，輸血才得以實現。導覽員也提醒我們，未經處理的水可能帶有病菌。離開博物館時，我對科學多了一份敬意。

questions.questionZh: 為什麼科學家必須不斷更新流感疫苗？
options: 因為疫苗每年都會漲價
因為流感病毒每年都會變化
因為疫苗放太久就會過期

questions.questionZh: 出口附近的海報在感謝誰？

items.promptZh: 有些藥必須透過靜脈注射給予。
referenceEn: Some medicines must be given by intravenous injection.
Some medicines have to be given through an intravenous line.
rubricZh: intravenous 是形容詞，後面接名詞（例如 intravenous injection）
「必須」可寫 must、have to 等；被動（例如 must be given）、主動（例如 Doctors must give…）都可以

items.promptZh: 這座湖裡住著許多肉眼看不見的微生物。
referenceEn: Many microorganisms that you cannot see with the naked eye live in this lake.
This lake is home to many microorganisms that are too small to see.
rubricZh: microorganism 指「微生物」，這裡用複數 microorganisms
「肉眼看不見的」可寫，例如 that you cannot see with the naked eye、too small to see 等
「住著」可寫，例如 live in、is home to 等
